findings.title: Falsy-default on success_statuses silently restores {200, 201} for an empty set
findings.problem: `expected_statuses = success_statuses or {200, 201}` uses truthiness, not a None check. The parameter is typed `set[int] | None`, so an explicitly-passed empty set (`success_statuses=set()`, a plausible way to express 'no status is acceptable') is falsy and silently falls back to the default `{200, 201}`, accepting statuses the caller meant to reject. The guard should be `if success_statuses is None`. No current caller passes an empty set — the only call site in-hunk passes `{200, 202, 204}` — so this is latent, not live, but it is a real mismatch between the declared `| None` contract and the implemented check.
findings.fix_hint: use `expected_statuses = {200, 201} if success_statuses is None else success_statuses`
findings.why_it_matters: The signature promises None-means-default, but the code means falsy-means-default. A future caller passing an empty or computed-empty set gets silently permissive status handling instead of the strict behavior it asked for.

findings.problem: The SlskdTransferClient class docstring is now factually stale relative to its own API surface. It states "Exposes only the download enqueue (POST) and status fetch (GET) endpoints on the /api/v0/transfers/downloads surface", but the class now also exposes cancel_download (DELETE) on that same surface. This docstring is load-bearing in this codebase, not decorative: it is the human-readable half of the dry-run safety boundary whose machine-readable half is assert_search_only_operation in src/roonseek/slskd.py:214 (with _FORBIDDEN_SEGMENTS = {"downloads", "transfers"}). The two clients are deliberately split so the search client can never reach transfer endpoints; the transfer client's contract is documented purely in prose. A reader auditing the acquisition boundary now gets a docstring that under-reports the client's write capability, and DELETE is the most destructive verb on it.

findings.title: cancel_download will be called with the local SQLite transfers.id, not the slskd transfer GUID — cancel is a no-op against real slskd
findings.problem: The new `cancel_download(username, transfer_id)` boundary is correct in isolation, but nothing in this repo can supply a real slskd transfer id. `transfers` (src/roonseek/schema.sql:341-353) has columns id/wanted_album_id/username/folder_path/filename/size_bytes/state — there is NO column holding slskd's per-file transfer GUID, and the pipeline never captures one: `_inspect_transfer_status` (src/roonseek/pipeline.py:723-780) reads only `filename`, `state`, and `bytesTransferred` out of each slskd file dict, discarding `id`. The RED test for the consumer confirms the wiring the plan intends: tests/test_jobs_api.py asserts `fake.calls == [("alice", str(transfer_id))]` where `transfer_id` is the local SQLite rowid returned by `_seed_active_acquisition`. Against a live slskd this produces DELETE /api/v0/transfers/downloads/alice/1, which slskd will answer 404 (or silently no-op) rather than cancelling the real transfer. The operator sees the acquisition marked `cancelled` in the DB and the staging directory deleted, while slskd keeps downloading into a directory that was just removed. This is a correctness gap in the phase's contract, not in the HTTP verb handling. pending: confirm slskd's DELETE-by-id semantics against the deployed slskd version and confirm plan 22-03's intended id source.
findings.fix_hint: Persist slskd's per-file transfer id: capture `transfer.get("id")` in _inspect_transfer_status, add a `remote_transfer_id` column to the transfers table (+ migration), and have the cancel action pass that value rather than the local rowid.
findings.why_it_matters: Cancel appears to succeed (200, status=cancelled, directory deleted) while the download continues server-side. Divergence between UI state and slskd reality is exactly the class of bug per-item acquisition control exists to eliminate, and the deleted staging directory means the still-running transfer writes to a path that no longer exists.

findings.title: success_statuses widens the accepted-status set for a shared helper without narrowing the 2xx floor — 204 now bypasses the JSON contract for future callers
findings.problem: `_request_json` gained a `success_statuses` keyword. The default `{200, 201}` preserves existing behavior for enqueue_download and get_user_downloads, so this change is backward compatible today (verified: the only two other call sites, transfer.py:187 and :197, pass no override). The residual risk is shape drift rather than breakage: `success_statuses or {200, 201}` treats an explicitly-passed empty set as "use the default" (falsy), so a caller writing `success_statuses=set()` silently gets 200/201 accepted instead of nothing. Note also the divergence from the sibling client: slskd.py:_request_json rejects any status >= 400 and hard-requires a Mapping payload, while transfer.py now accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied set and returns {} on empty body. The two clients' error contracts are drifting apart, which matters because the codebase deliberately keeps them as parallel boundaries.
